summary.headline: Trishakti FY26 revenue rose ~90% to INR 32.44 crore, but EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore subvention income and receivables sit near 200 days.
summary.overview: Trishakti reported FY26 revenue of about INR 32.44 crore (up ~90% YoY), EBITDA of INR 20.21 crore (62% margin) and PAT of INR 7.66 crore (25% margin), with Q4 revenue above three times YoY. Reported EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore of subvention income booked under other income, which management calls operating in nature. Fresh capex was INR 210 crore against ~INR 100 crore guidance, taking the fleet to over 140 machines. Management said FY27 order book is INR 60-62 crore, but trade receivables (~200 days) and debt-to-equity (near 2:1) remain the key open items.

segments.name: Crane / heavy equipment rental (sole business)
segments.commentary: Management describes the company as a pure-play rental platform with 140+ machines and near-full utilisation, serving L&T, Reliance, Tata, RVNL and NCC. Gross yield is ~3% per month and targeted ROC is 22-25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crane hiring revenue projection of INR 62.5 crore and INR 95 crore in FY28 is shown in the investor presentation; management says INR 33 crore of FY26 is an actual and FY27 billing run-rate is ~INR 5 crore per month.
FY27 order book stated at INR 60-62 crore, excluding variable overtime; contracts run to 31 December on paper and management expects extensions.
Target ROC 22-25%; management says ROC guidance is conservative because the INR 400 crore capex will not be full-year.
Management expects receivables to normalise in FY27 after a family settlement is cleared; expects debt-to-equity to settle around 1.5 over time.
Fleet target for next phase is 50-250 ton machines for the first ~INR 400 crore of capex, to keep utilisation above 95%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR 210 crore against INR 100 crore guidance; roughly INR 150 crore of machines bought in H2 alone.
Fleet grew from eight machines (FY24) to over 140 machines; plan is to reach north of 200 machines.
About INR 27-28 crore of machines moved out of CWIP recently; management says CWIP is now zero.
Revenue lags capex by 1-1.5 months (compliance, transport, TPI); management says FY28 will show a 12-month run-rate.
Repays ~2.5% of loans monthly; expects to add ~INR 100 crore of borrowing as repayments of INR 40-45 crore accrue.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives new RFQs daily for 250-750 ton machines and sees no demand slowdown.
Cited Reliance's Kutch renewable expansion (civil work done, cranes expected in next 2-3 months) as an example.
Yields of ~3% monthly are said to apply to machines below 100 tons; higher-tonnage machines have lower yield but higher margin.
Management says the company works with tier-1 clients only; tier-2/3 EPC payment cycles can exceed five months.
Management says it is not working with government bodies and is focusing on private capex.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for crane and rental demand over 2-3 years, and any signs of slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no slowdown and expects demand to rise; availability of 500+ ton machines may constrain growth, so near-term focus is 50-250 ton machines.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days still ~200 with tier-1 clients, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to a small family settlement from 2023 and a INR 1 crore written-off inter-company receivable; says it will normalise in FY27. Under-six-month receivables are said to be about 45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unbilled revenue rise from ~INR 2 crore to ~INR 4.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says fleet doubled H1 to H2 (from ~INR 125 crore to ~INR 250 crore), and bill submission takes 20-22 days due to client compliance; management says unbilled will always be present and there is no bad-debt risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is subvention income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management describes it as a financing arrangement between OEM banks and the NBFC, passed to the company as interest waivers; it is booked in Q4 because Q1-Q3 were unaudited. Management calls it part of core hiring business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall below the 60% benchmark in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says other income is part of core hiring; margins are stable on an adjusted basis. An analyst computed ~58% including subvention in revenue, versus a September quarter level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it bought INR 60-65 crore of machines in Q4, paying 20-25 days of advance labour and 3-7 days for gate passes; other expenses rose from spares for FY24 machines as free-of-cost service periods ended.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 leverage and debt-to-equity capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity will remain around 1.5 to 2 times equity and that it intends to stay below 2 times; cost of borrowing is ~5% flat.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are ~3% monthly yields as competition rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says yields are sustainable, with the 3% mark applying mainly to sub-100 ton machines and blended yields holding up.

risks_watch: Trade receivables of ~200 days; management promises FY27 normalisation tied to a family settlement.
Debt-to-equity near 2:1, with ~INR 159 crore of payables/other liabilities expected to shift to borrowings; the timing and amount are not quantified.
Subvention income of INR 4.58 crore (about 23% of FY26 EBITDA) is complex and was booked in Q4; management offered to explain it off-call.
Margin sensitivity to capex-driven costs (labour pre-deployment, spares) and revenue lag of 1-1.5 months.
Contract tenure on paper only to 31 December; management expects extensions but has not confirmed them.
Machine availability for 500+ ton machines and operational downtime risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and FY27 growth, but evasive on specifics such as debt levels, receivables and subvention mechanics, repeatedly deferring to post-call discussions.
key_quotes: So whatever the unbilled amount is there, it is actually a calculation of our hourly rates into the hours machines have already worked in those very days.
The demand side is not the issue for us. It's just that the availability of the machines will be an issue for us in future when it comes to more than 500 tons of machine.
Our reported EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crores of subvention income classified under other income. However, we view this as operating in nature.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR 290 crore (net asset base); ~INR 260 crore (assets, as stated in call)
~INR 159 crore (as cited by analyst; ~INR 150 crore machine-related)

adds.what: Fleet of crane/heavy equipment machines grew to over 140 machines; plan to reach north of 200 machines
Next phase: 50-250 ton machines funded by first ~INR 400 crore of capex

growth.why: Management guides FY27 crane hiring revenue of INR 62.5 crore (vs INR 33 crore FY26) and INR 95 crore in FY28, backed by an FY27 order book of INR 60-62 crore, daily RFQs and a fleet of 140+ machines with ~INR 400 crore further capex, but the brief gives no utilisation figure and receivables near 200 days and the subvention-inflated EBITDA weaken the quality of support.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell below the 60% benchmark (analyst computed ~58% incl. subvention) as INR 60-65 crore of Q4 machine purchases brought 20-25 days of advance labour and spares costs, and reported 62% FY26 margin is flattered by INR 4.58 crore subvention (~23% of EBITDA).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fleet already grew from 8 to 140+ machines with ~INR 150 crore bought in H2 FY26 and CWIP now zero; plan is to reach 200+ machines with the first ~INR 400 crore of capex, and management says FY28 will show a 12-month run-rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Crane hiring revenue guided to INR 62.5 crore in FY27 (vs INR 33 crore FY26) and INR 95 crore in FY28, with FY27 order book at INR 60-62 crore, daily RFQs and a monthly billing run-rate of ~INR 5 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fleet is near-full utilisation with 140+ machines, and management has a planned ~INR 400 crore capex phase for 50-250 ton machines targeting above 95% utilisation, plus ~INR 100 crore of new borrowing expected as repayments accrue.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR 62.5 crore revenue is set against an FY27 monthly run-rate of ~INR 5 crore (about INR 60 crore annualised), so it is roughly in line rather than clearly conservative; upside depends on the 20-day revenue lag and contract extensions beyond 31 December that management expects but has not confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables at ~200-205 days, debt-to-equity near 2:1, and contracts on paper only to 31 December, with ~INR 159 crore of payables expected to shift to borrowings and the timing unquantified.

rows.label: Receivables normalisation to ~45 days
rows.why: Trade receivables are ~200-205 days; management says FY27 normalisation is tied to clearing a family settlement, and under-six-month receivables are ~45 days, but no amount or date is quantified.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity held near 1.5 and below 2x
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is near 2:1 with ~INR 65 crore non-current borrowings and ~INR 100 crore of planned new borrowing, so the 1.5x target depends on equity growth and the unquantified shift of ~INR 159 crore payables into debt.

rows.label: Crane demand from renewables and infrastructure
rows.why: Management reports daily RFQs for 250-750 ton machines and cites Reliance Kutch renewable cranes expected within 2-3 months, with the FY27 order book at INR 60-62 crore excluding variable overtime.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, RFQs and fleet growth but evasive on receivables, debt levels and subvention mechanics, deferring to off-call discussions; analysts pressed on the 62% margin, subvention income and Q4 margin dip.
